Device for generating radial push force by utilizing centrifugal force - China patent

#ufotwitter

Core Concept

The invention is based on the principle of manipulating centrifugal force generated by a rotating mass that is unbalanced relative to its axis of rotation (an "eccentric rotating body"). By controlling the speed and the rotational phase of this unbalanced mass, the device aims to produce a continuous, directional radial push force.

Technical Mechanism

Asymmetric Design: The rotating body (the "decentral swivel") has a weight distribution that is intentionally uneven on either side of its rotation axis. This is achieved by creating one side of the body with a solid, high-density construction and the other with a hollow, lower-density structure.

Variable Speed Control: The system requires a high-torque power unit capable of precise, rapid changes in rotational speed (angular velocity).

Thrust Generation: The device produces radial thrust by dynamically varying the rotational speed depending on the position of the heavy side of the swivel. By accelerating the swivel when the heavier side is moving toward a target direction and decelerating it as it moves away, the system attempts to create a net directional force vector.

Intended Application

The patent suggests potential applications in fields requiring propulsion, such as aviation and space flight, specifically mentioning the possibility of vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) systems and manned spacecraft. The inventor argues that this method could provide more efficient thrust than traditional chemical fuel propulsion and offer better control over acceleration and deceleration.

Some small percentage of UFOs also use this type of Centrifugal propulsion, it's not just MHD, field resonance, or those based on plasma actuators.
